title: e-Ustad: Negotiation Skills
description: Negotiation is a process of communication and interaction between two or more parties who have differing interests, goals, or viewpoints. The primary objective of negotiation is to reach a mutually acceptable agreement or resolution that addresses the concerns and needs of all parties involved. Negotiation is a crucial skill for law enforcement professionals, as it plays a significant role in resolving conflicts, managing crises, and ensuring public safety. Law enforcement officers today face a myriad of challenges that extend beyond the realm of enforcing laws. As societies become more complicated, officers need to change the way they handle things. They have to learn how to handle arguments, calm down tense situations, and work with different groups of people. Sometimes, simply using their power and authority isn't enough. This is where negotiation skills come into play. By honing these skills, officers can navigate complex interactions with greater finesse, leading to peaceful resolution that prioritises both public safety and individual rights. Law enforcement officers furthermore often encounter high-stress situations that require rapid decision- making. Effective negotiation skills can de-escalate volatile situations by allowing officers to establish rapport, understand the emotions and motivations of those involved, and find non-violent solutions. This can prevent conflicts from spiralling into violent confrontations, minimising harm to all parties.
provider: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: e-Ustad: POCSO Act
description: Child Sexual Abuse (CSA) is a grave violation of human rights and poses a serious threat to the well-being and safety of children. It is the most heinous crime against children and in most instances, it is hidden in nature and also it is the most under-reported crime. CSA is largely ignored by the public and criminal justice system. In India, CSA was not publicly acknowledged as a criminal offence. It was only after the enactment of new legislation called 'The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act)' that criminalised a range of acts including child rape, harassment and exploitation of pornography. The POCSO Act is a dedicated legal framework designed to address the alarming issue of CSA. India is home to over 19% of the world's children or 42% (more than one-third) of India's total population. Approx. 50% of these children are in need of care and protection. The POCSO Act is a landmark legislation that specifically focuses on the protection of children from sexual offences. It defines a child as any person below the age of 18 years and recognises the unique vulnerability of children to sexual abuse and exploitation. It aims to create a safe and secure environment for children by preventing and punishing those who commit sexual offences against them.
provider: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: e-Ustad: Soft Skills and Communication Skills
description: The police department is one of the most important institutions in any society. The police are primarily responsible for maintaining public safety by enforcing laws, protecting lives and property, and providing emergency assistance when needed. However, in recent years, the police have faced increased criticism for their handling of various situations. One of the primary issues is the lack of soft skills. Soft skills refer to interpersonal skills that enable individuals to communicate effectively, work collaboratively, and build relationships with others. These skills are crucial in the context of policing because police officers regularly interact with people from diverse backgrounds and cultures. According to research conducted at Harvard and Stanford Universities, only 15% of your career success is provided by your hard skills, while the other 85% is provided by so-called soft skills. 'Soft Skills' correlates with some terms of very close meaning: 'Life Skills', 'Emotional Intelligence Quotients', 'Social Skills' and 'Interpersonal Skills'. Further, the soft skills are broken down into categories, or types of skills according to the level of complexity and interaction. A learner needs to go through this e-learning course on Soft Skills and Communication Skills for knowing more.

This course on Computer Based Interlocking System (CBI) is designed and developed by Signaling and Train Control (S&TC) team of Delhi Metro Rail Academy of Delhi Metro. 
This course is developed for providing an introduction to the Computer Based Interlocking systems for metro trains around the world.
 In Metro signaling, an interlocking is an arrangement of various signal apparatus that prevents conflicting movements of trains.  An interlocking is so designed that it is impossible to display a signal to proceed unless the route to be used is proven safe. Interlocking is a safety measure designed to prevent signals and points/switches from being changed in an improper sequence. For example, interlocking would prevent a signal from being changed to indicate a diverging route, unless the corresponding points/switches had been changed first. 
The interlocking System shall provide all the Control and Indication functions as per approved Selection Table and Panel Diagram of the Station.

title: E-Learning Modules on Basics of the Underwater World (Part-2)
description: In the second part of the course, the focus shifts towards advanced aspects of Underwater Domain Awareness (UDA) and its practical applications. The curriculum covers the Underwater Data Analytics Framework, providing insights into acoustic propagation in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and addressing underwater channel modeling, simulation, and field validation. Additionally, the course explores underwater robotics, including their challenges and opportunities, offering foundational knowledge, classification of applications, and insights into various types of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) and their design and development considerations. The discussion also extends to underwater deployment, emphasizing different deployment types, their applications, and the influence of tropical characteristics on sensor performance and safety. The course further addresses acoustic habitat degradation and management, highlighting underwater acoustics, sources of underwater noise, and marine spatial planning, with real-world examples such as Bubble Feeding by Big Whales. It concludes by examining the role of digital transformation in enhancing coastal communities' livelihoods. This encompasses the digital ocean, the development of an APY analysis tool for seaweed cultivation and shrimp farming, as well as the governance perspective and challenges associated with the APY Tool. These five segments provide advanced insights into UDA, from data analytics and underwater robotics to digital transformation, expanding participants' understanding of the multifaceted world of underwater domain awareness.

title: E-Learning Modules on Basics of the Underwater World (Part-1)
description: This comprehensive course on Underwater Domain Awareness (UDA) covers a wide spectrum of topics vital to understanding UDA's role in contemporary maritime contexts. It begins with a foundational exploration of UDA, emphasizing its significance and key stakeholders. The course then delves into the strategic alignment of the UDA Framework with India's SAGAR vision, offering insights into India's global positioning and various projects that complement this vision. Next, it addresses the intricacies of UDA in tropical waters, considering political, economic, and historical challenges, while contextualizing UDA within the evolving Indo-Pacific strategy. The course also emphasizes sustainability concerns in the Indian Ocean, encompassing issues such as acoustic habitat degradation, IUU fishing, pollution, and ecosystem degradation, all within the context of India's unique tropical characteristics. Finally, it highlights the need for effective maritime governance and the imperative of a UDA framework. This section discusses regulatory challenges, decision-making dynamics, and the role of the scientific community in managing underwater domains. By encompassing these five modules, the course provides participants with a holistic and in-depth understanding of UDA's significance and its critical role in shaping maritime security and sustainability in the modern world.

title: ATAL BHUJAL YOJANA
description:
The government and policy makers have recognized the potential of community led groundwater management and the need to institutionalize such initiatives through convergence of Govt. initiatives with emphasis on demand side management and behavioural change for ensuring the long-term sustainability of ground water in the country. Atal Bhujal Yojana is a major step in this direction with an earmark of Rs.6, 000 crores to be implemented over a period of five years (2020-21 till 2024-25) for sustainable management of groundwater. This is the first scheme of its kind which will involve community based planning; monitoring; sharing and use of ground water data; capacity building of all stakeholders to demystify the complex science of ground water; community led groundwater management through a combination of demand side / supply side management measures. The program is being executed by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, and it is being financed by the Government of India and the World Bank on a proportion of 50:50 basis.

Objectives
	To demonstrate community-led sustainable ground water management which can be taken to scale. 
	To improve the management of groundwater resources in select water stressed areas in identified states viz. Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
	Sustainable ground water management, mainly through convergence among various on-going schemes with the active involvement of local communities and stakeholders. Ensuring judicious utilization of funds allocated by the Central and State governments for long term sustainability of ground water resources. 
	Creation of strong data base, scientific approach and community participation. 
	Strengthening the institutional framework for participatory groundwater management. 
	Bringing about behavioural change at the community level through awareness programs and capacity building for fostering sustainable groundwater management in the participating States.

title: Time Management
description:
During the industrial revolution and the rise of factory work, people “had to learn to live by the clock rather than by the sun.”In 1911, Frederick Winslow Taylor published “The Principles of Scientific Management” in which he proposed the concept of time management.  Taylor was concerned with reducing process time and worked with factory managers on scientific time studies. 
At its most basic level, time studies involve breaking down each job into component parts, timing each element, and rearranging the parts into the most efficient method of working.
Managers and superiors play an important role in inculcating time management skills in employees and so must lead by example. The best way to finish work on time is to be punctual at workplace.

title: Personal and Organizational Value
description:
Values are our beliefs we work and live with. Values determine our priorities and guide our behaviour. Everyone has values but each person has a different value set. Organisational values are a set of core beliefs held by an organisation. These are guiding principles that provide an organisation with purpose and direction and set the tone for its interactions with its stakeholders, employees and others. Organisational values provide a common purpose that all employees should understand, work towards and live by.

employing knowledge from various disciplines in an integrated manner – or at
least it is a multidisciplinary form of research, which applies the insights from
different disciplines to one and the same subject.

three other distinctive features. These unique features all influence the way in
which research is conducted.

title: Butterfly Diversity and Identification
description: Butterflies are vivid expressions of life and since time immemorial have inspired writers, poets, artists and naturalists throughout the globe. “Rabindranath Tagore once wrote- The butterfly counts not months but moments, and has time enough”. “The fluttering of a butterfly's wings can effect climate changes on the other side of the planet” by Paul Erlich, is a more recent quote. India has extremely diverse terrain, climate and vegetation, which comprises extremes of heat cold, desert and jungles, of low-lying plains and the highest mountains, of dryness and dampness, islands and continental areas, widely varying flora, and sharply marked seasons.  In addition, India hosts three of the world's biodiversity hotspots: the Western Ghats, the Eastern Himalayas, and the hilly ranges bordering India and Myanmar, each having numerous endemic species. Accordingly, India's diverse and varied fauna include a rich variety of butterflies.  In 1932, Brigadier William Harry Evans recorded approximately 1439 species of butterfly from British India, and now ~1700 taxa of butterflies are known  from India.  Butterflies are also ecologically important because of the role they play in the food chain of a forest ecosystem. Their egg, larva (caterpillars) and adult (butterfly) form the food of a number of other animals. Most butterflies are pollinators of flowering plants and have a symbiotic relationship with plant diversity as they are dependent upon a variety of plants for larval food. Butterflies are also good biological indicators of environmental variation and quality. Ecotourism with butterflies in parks, gardens and  conservatories has recently gained much importance and widely practiced in many countries across the tropics. Keeping all these aspects in mind it has now become important for us to know about and identify butterflies in our neighborhood. This course  is designed for beginners to make them aware about various aspects of butterflies and guide them in identification
